guardrails-poc.title: Guardrail PoC, end to end
guardrails-poc.sub: Vendor reports never tested our own business, so I ran 3,600 questions against an add-on guardrail and advised sticking with the built-in defence for now.
guardrails-poc.role: Led the bank's side of the PoC: wrote the questions, ran and analysed tests, made the call
guardrails-poc.outcome: XecGuard done, advice: do not buy it yet; Vulcan still in testing

items.name: Define the question
items.desc: Six policies mapped to FSC rules
points: The vendor reports looked good, but none had tested KGI's own business
I listed the six policy types XecGuard had switched on and mapped them to FSC principles 2 to 5
One question only: can it stop attacks aimed at KGI without blocking customers' normal questions?

items.name: Build the questions
points: Following the OWASP AI Testing Guide, I built three question sets, 3,600 questions in all
The 1,100 domain questions cover the wealth app's 10 business areas, each tied to a real API field
Attack to normal questions run 4:1, each tagged with a risk level, and the set is version-controlled

items.name: Two test rounds
items.desc: R1 and R2, logged per question
points: R1 ran all 3,600 with only the six policies; R2 added a system prompt and custom rules, then reran
It blocked 98.3% of red-team prompts, but also 20 of 30 normal questions, adding about 0.8 s each
Custom policies worked: on 1,500 questions the miss rate fell from 10.2% to 2.2%

items.name: Nine-part comparison
points: I scored XecGuard and the platform's built-in defence on the same nine-part evaluation sheet
XecGuard scored only 62.5/100; the built-in defence had already blocked every attack in the same set
Vulcan: 1,330 red-team benchmark prompts across 44 risk types, 73.4 for validation coverage

items.name: Recommendation
points: An extra layer would block no more, wrongly block more, and need its own integration and fees
The 3,600-question set stays, so every future Agent is accepted against the same yardstick
Next: finish the Vulcan PoC and set pass marks for missed attacks and wrongly blocked questions

agentic-platform-eval.title: Pre-purchase issue funnel
agentic-platform-eval.sub: A wrong platform often shows its gaps halfway through, so I tested both candidates before purchase, found 12 issues and scored them side by side.
agentic-platform-eval.role: Led the evaluation: designed and ran the tests, logged issues, filled in the scores
agentic-platform-eval.outcome: 12 issues found before purchase, 4 of them launch blockers

items.name: Two candidates
points: Four business Agents need a platform; pick wrong and a key feature may be missing halfway through
The question was not which has more features, but which will not break in our use cases

items.name: 60 hands-on tests
points: I designed Dify's tests around its own five modules, after collecting known issues from its GitHub
The bank's 238 regulatory and 119 penalty Q&As tested its knowledge base, sources and hallucination
On Agatha I ran 26 tests and tagged every issue by severity

items.name: 12 issues
points: Agatha's 26 tests turned up 12 issues, all found before purchase
Sorted into three grades: launch blockers, security issues and general issues

items.name: 4 blockers
points: Of the 12 issues, 4 would have kept an Agent from launching
One more was a security hole, caught now instead of after launch

items.name: Basis for the pick
points: Both platforms were scored on the group's 42-item, nine-category sheet and on our department's sheet
My PoC report and scorecards are what the group used to choose its platform
Once chosen, the guardrail question set and pre-launch checks apply to every Agent built on it

agent-cost-roi.title: Four Agents, one cost lens
agent-cost-roi.sub: The four Agents serve different people and spend money differently, so I built four prototypes and one shared cost-benefit formula to compare them side by side.
agent-cost-roi.role: Built all four prototypes and led the shared cost-benefit framework
agent-cost-roi.outcome: Four working prototypes; three-year baselines being built

items.name: Four prototypes
points: Each Agent covers one stage of the customer journey: acquisition, transaction, service, wealth
I made each one a working prototype, so business units could see and try it before investing
The wealth assistant, for example, is a mobile banking MVP, from login to chatting with the AI

items.name: Shared formula
points: Cost = volume × usage per case × unit price, and benefit works the same way
Cloud or on-prem, billed per call or per case, all become cost per case and ROI
Business ratios show whether AI is doing the work; realisation ratios show whether forecasts came true

items.name: Three-year baseline
points: Business units supply volumes; IT supplies usage
Once the data is in, I build a three-year volume, cost and benefit baseline for each Agent
Small internal requests use a simpler scorecard instead: benefit, feasibility, compliance and cost

result.name: Side by side
points: For the first time, all four Agents fit in one comparison table
After launch, a realisation ratio below the threshold triggers a review of resources or scope
The AI operations platform now runs this comparison, with plan and actual side by side

notes.text: Benefit too: volume × value per case × unit value

agent-loan-assistant.title: Loan assistant, layer by layer
agent-loan-assistant.sub: Applicants left when no one answered, so I built a prototype that chats, guides the application and negotiates within limits, tied to the cost framework.
agent-loan-assistant.role: Built the prototype and brought it into the four Agents' shared cost framework
agent-loan-assistant.outcome: Prototype works end to end; baseline waits on business volumes

items.name: Three channels
points: Applicants with questions often left when no one answered right away
Desktop and mobile application sites plus a mock LINE account all run the same assistant
After accepting a quote on LINE, a customer jumps straight to the application site to continue

items.name: Guided application
points: Personal, mortgage and car loan pages with calculators, plus a four-step application
If an application stalls on a step, the assistant checks in, winning back people who drift away

items.name: Negotiation in limits
points: The base rate follows the pre-screen grade, and within its authority the assistant concedes in small steps
Beyond its authority it raises a pricing request; the manager's approval or counter-offer returns to the chat
Human-on-the-loop: it acts alone within limits and hands exceptions to a person

items.name: Guardrails & privacy
points: An output guardrail blocks lines like "guaranteed approval", and every quote shows the total-cost APR
Code, not the model, works out rates and payments; text is de-identified before the cloud, with a daily cap

items.name: Hand-off to credit
points: A submitted application exports as a case pack, with document images, for the credit review Agent
Tested: the credit Agent imports it, reads the images and works out annual income
A 12-page back office, plus automated tests for pricing limits and the full end-to-end flow

items.name: Cost and benefit
points: Its value is in how many applications it helps close, not hours saved
Business ratio: AI-assisted applications ÷ all applications, plus the conversion rate
I have asked the business unit for volumes; the three-year baseline follows once they arrive

notes.text: never promises approval · rates come from code

agent-credit-review.title: Credit review pipeline
agent-credit-review.sub: Underwriters checked papers one by one, slowly and unevenly, so I built a prototype that reads them, checks them and works out income, then priced each case.
agent-credit-review.role: Built the prototype and led its cost-benefit assessment
agent-credit-review.outcome: 96.6% field accuracy; three-year cost baseline done

items.name: Intake
points: Underwriters checked income papers and worked out income by hand, slowly and unevenly
My generator makes 6 kinds of synthetic papers with skew, noise and stamps, each with a known answer
It also imports the case packs sent over by the loan assistant

items.name: OCR
points: Local OCR stands in for on-prem by default, and a cloud vision model can be swapped in
A date or amount it cannot read is cropped and read again
Field accuracy: 96.6% on the 12-person test set, 97.7% on the demo cases

items.name: Checks & income
points: It cross-checks payslips, withholding slips and bank deposits against each other
Income comes with the rules, formula and reasons used; every test and demo case was right
Every problem planted in the documents was found

items.name: Human review
points: Unsure cases go to a person, and any change by an underwriter needs a reason
No approval advice or credit score is shown, so the decision stays with people
All 4 fairness pairs got identical results

items.name: Cost baseline
points: I split the flow into on-prem reading and cloud processing, costing each in its closest unit
From case volumes and three-year growth forecasts I worked out cost per case and a three-year baseline
Work runs in off-peak batches; next, add build and upkeep costs to finish TCO and ROI

notes.text: all runs in an off-peak batch

agent-customer-service.title: Service Copilot model
agent-customer-service.sub: Call agents searched mid-call and wrote notes after, so I built an AI sidekick prototype that finds facts, drafts replies and sums up calls; people sign off.
agent-customer-service.role: Contributor: built the prototype and cost framework; a colleague led computing estimates
agent-customer-service.outcome: Prototype works; waiting on the vendor's updated computing estimate

center.name: Service agent
points: The agent faces the customer while AI helps from behind and never replies directly
The agent reads any draft aloud in their own words and confirms everything saved to the record

items.name: Synthetic calls
points: I made 12 calls with computer voices: lost cards, billing disputes, suspected fraud and more
Two channels split agent and customer, and no real customer data is in any recording

items.name: Live transcript
points: Local Whisper runs by default and tells speakers apart by channel
Word error rate was about 14%, and speaker and call-type labels were all correct

items.name: KB suggestions
points: Knowledge-base tips update with the call, beside customer details with personal data masked
It drafts a reply first, and the agent decides what to say

items.name: Summary & QA
points: After the call AI writes a summary; it is saved only once the agent confirms, masked again first
QA scores each item on a rubric and sends serious issues to a supervisor; no full card number appeared

items.name: All on-prem
points: Because it handles call recordings and personal data, everything runs in the bank's own data centre
In on-prem-only mode, the service refuses to start if it finds any cloud address

items.name: Cost framework
points: Speech and text are measured in different units, so I turned both into a service cost per call
The call-volume baseline is done; after a first computing meeting, we are waiting on the vendor

agent-wealth-assistant.title: Wealth assistant, end to end
agent-wealth-assistant.sub: Customers dug through many accounts to see what they own, so I led the PoC and resource plan and built a banking prototype where one question checks it all.
agent-wealth-assistant.role: Led the PoC and launch resource planning, and built the prototype myself
agent-wealth-assistant.outcome: Working 118-page banking prototype; launch handed to the next team

items.name: PoC
points: Customers had to dig through each account to piece together what they own
A PoC came first, confirming the AI assistant could answer questions

items.name: Architecture hand-off
items.desc: Draft passed to a senior dev
points: I drew the first system architecture and wrote up the test results and documents
Then handed development to a senior colleague

items.name: Banking prototype
points: From the specs I built a mobile and web banking MVP with 118 working pages
Transfers, FX and fund orders all post to a mock bank, and the AI's answers update at once

items.name: AI assistant
points: It calls 36 account tools over MCP, covering 240 fields
It gets the risk level before recommending anything, never trades, never touches passwords or codes
Following A2UI v0.9 it adds charts to answers, and passes every official test case

items.name: Five gates
points: 31 input rules and 32 output rules, plus personal-data masking
An on-prem small model reads intent, and the model never sees any balance
It keeps only short-term memory, and only the masked version

items.name: Launch prep
points: From login numbers I forecast three years of usage and sized production and test environments
It is the heaviest user of the four Agents; the team that took it over drives the launch
After launch, the metric is activity: people using AI chat ÷ people logging in

ai-ops-platform.title: The operations iceberg
ai-ops-platform.sub: The four Agents' numbers sat in four back offices, so I built one platform for operations and journeys; it caught plan and actual measured in different ways.
ai-ops-platform.role: Led design and build of the data contract, the platform and all four Agent exports
ai-ops-platform.outcome: All four prototypes connected; business plans revised to version 2

items.name: One platform
points: Answering "is it worth it, what does it cost" used to mean four back offices and manual conversion
Five modules: overview, customer journey, cost and performance, business plans, governance
The report site is read-only and only the admin site can change things, both behind Zero Trust

items.name: Plan vs actual
items.desc: Side by side, with hit rates
points: Plans cover a 2026 pilot and 2027 to 2029, shown beside the actuals
The very first comparison had three numbers several times apart
After fixes, only Agents truly behind are flagged, like the loan assistant below its own 80% bar

items.name: Data contract
points: No shared code: each Agent follows one format and opens a read-only export
Exports need a key and accept only internal calls; if the platform stops, the Agents carry on

items.name: Hashed journeys
points: All four Agents hash customer IDs with the same key
The four stages join into one customer's timeline, yet the hash cannot be reversed to an identity
I walked one test customer through all four Agents and fixed a time-zone bug that misordered intake

items.name: One yardstick
points: Agents report only usage, and the platform prices it from one rate card
Real data only; under 5 cases it shows a count, not a percentage

items.name: Fixing definitions
points: Loan benefit: actual counted all assisted applications, the plan only the 18% AI drove
Service per-call cost left out speech recognition; credit history kept amounts but no usage
I added a benefit basis and split variable from fixed cost; the plans were approved as version 2

agent-governance.title: Nine-cell launch check
agent-governance.sub: The regulator's principles were clear but no one could say how to check them, so I broke them into a nine-cell table: fill every cell with proof to pass.
agent-governance.role: Led the design of the bank's pre-launch AI check
agent-governance.outcome: Survey and framework done; data collection under way, pilot next

items.name: Six principles
points: Accountability, fairness, privacy, robustness and safety, transparency, sustainability
Four Agents were about to launch, yet no one could say how to check them

items.name: Three layers
points: I split checks into three layers: documents, the AI's output and the AI's behaviour
The survey showed existing rules covered only documents; output and behaviour were blank

items.name: Nine-cell table
points: The examiners' eight items really ask three things: assessed? recorded? still managed?
Three layers by three questions make nine cells; fill all with proof to pass

items.name: Five-step check
points: It sits after risk assessment and before approval: scope, rules, questions, testing, report
Chat, decision, generative and scoring AI each get their own test, sharing one bar: zero serious errors

items.name: Pilot and rulebook
points: Business units are now answering how each of the four Agents maps to the six principles
The loan assistant pilots it first, then it goes into the bank's AI lifecycle rules
It starts at SIT/UAT, and nothing reaches production without a check report

notes.text: pass = zero severe errors · no report, no production
Survey: today only layer one is covered

finllm.title: Batch cleaning loop
finllm.sub: Bad training data teaches a finance model wrong, so I clean it item by item, score its regulatory answers, and turned the method into a standard process.
finllm.role: Contributor: cleaned the data and scored the model's regulatory answers

items.name: New batch
points: The FSC is backing FinLLM, and KGI takes part in data cleaning and model evaluation
The group sends one batch a week, with 9 more still to come

items.name: Clean each item
points: I clean, proofread and correct the raw data one item at a time
Batch 2-1 is done; the goal is to finish all cleaning by January 2027

items.name: Score rulings
items.desc: Did the model read it right?
points: I score the model's answers to regulatory questions to see if it understood them
Batch 4 is done and batch 5 is being scored

items.name: Standard process
points: I wrote the method up as fixed steps so it scales to more items
Once all batches are done, the model is evaluated as a whole and delivered on the group's schedule

notes.text: one item at a time; no shortcut

gemini-training.title: Scenario-led Gemini course
gemini-training.sub: Staff had the tool but not a sense of what to hand it, so I planned a course where each unit practises safety, tools and prompts on its own work.
gemini-training.role: Led the course design and gathered work scenarios from each unit
gemini-training.outcome: Outline final; scenarios being gathered, classes not yet run

center.name: Use it in my job
points: Handing out the tool is not enough; staff need to know which tasks suit AI
The course answers "how can my job use this", not "what can the tool do"

items.name: Set the outline
points: I agreed the outline with advisers around three topics: safety, tools and prompts
Safety answers the common worry about how to use AI without risk

items.name: Gather scenarios
points: I am collecting the tasks each business unit wants AI to help with
Classes will practise on them instead of generic examples; collection is ongoing

items.name: Run the classes
points: Once scenarios are in, classes run all three topics on each unit's own work
Prompts, the instructions given to AI, are written for real tasks

items.name: Track results
points: Afterwards I track attendance and how many AI use cases learners put forward
The second number shows whether people took the class back to their jobs

ai-ops-dashboard.title: Five AI value lenses
ai-ops-dashboard.sub: Every AI effort had its own numbers but none showed if it was worth it, so I helped design five shared lenses for internal tools and customer-facing Agents.
ai-ops-dashboard.role: Contributor: helped design the metrics and planned the cost and guardrail data feeds
ai-ops-dashboard.outcome: Five-lens framework done; dashboard still in planning

center.name: Worth it?
points: Copilot, Gemini and Ella inside, four Agents outside, each with its own numbers
Adoption and quality say whether it is used; benefit, cost and risk say whether it is worth it

items.name: Adoption
points: Licences, activation, active users and how many departments use it
Copilot is widening its trial: 25 departments have applied for 771 seats

items.name: Quality
points: Answer accuracy, hand-off-to-human rate and user feedback
Copilot's and Gemini's own vendor reports already carry usage data

items.name: Benefit
points: Internally, hours saved; externally, conversion for loans and throughput for credit review
Service cost for the call centre, activity and AUM for the wealth assistant

items.name: Cost
points: Licence fees, token usage and GPU usage
Customer-facing Agents reuse the four Agents' cost model

items.name: Risk
points: Missed-attack rate, false-block rate and incidents
Figures come from the miss and false-block rates measured in the Guardrails PoC

items.name: First monthly report
points: Next, confirm with IT what Copilot data exists and produce the first monthly report
Ella needs IT to open back-office access; then each metric gets a target

a2ui-research.title: A2UI path to product
a2ui-research.sub: Money answers came as long text that customers struggled with, so I am taking A2UI from technology to product in five stages and have picked three use cases.
a2ui-research.role: Led the research into whether it can become a bank product feature
a2ui-research.outcome: Stages one and two: use cases picked, resources being confirmed

items.name: Why A2UI
points: The Agent sends JSON naming components and data; the front end draws them from approved parts
AI decides the layout; the bank decides which components exist
It sends data, not code, which is what gives it a chance in security review

items.name: Business use cases
points: Built around the wealth assistant: asset overview, product comparison, form filling
Under the pre-launch check it cannot trade, so there are no order buttons

items.name: Resources
points: I listed environment specs, Azure AI Foundry and token requests, and IT test hookups
The approved component list decides what A2UI can draw; this is being confirmed

items.name: Value check
points: Technically possible is only the entry bar; the next gate is business value
With business units, agree which use case goes first and how success is measured

items.name: PoC and launch
points: Build the chosen case in a test environment under the guardrails and pre-launch check
Then schedule it with the wealth assistant team; the prototype already supports A2UI

zones.label: How: send a screen, not code

webai-finance.title: Research assistant iceberg
webai-finance.sub: Researchers first had to gather reports, macro data and news daily, so I took a module from requirements to launch alone: pick a market or stock, ask AI.
webai-finance.role: Owned the module and took it from requirements to launch on my own
webai-finance.outcome: Live; hard numbers on the impact to be added

items.name: Pick and ask
points: Pick a market or a stock and AI answers from curated data, with follow-ups
Researchers used to collect and sort reports and news themselves every day

items.name: Live in familiar UI
points: The assistant sits inside the interface people already use
Webai Finance is live, and time spent gathering data has gone down

items.name: Permissions
points: The hardest part was access: the tool is open to the whole group
Yet the asset manager's data had to stay walled off, so one design had to do both

items.name: Data feeds
points: Broker reports, macro data and news come in over SFTP
The PoC first proved AI could answer market and stock questions from them

items.name: Agent flow
points: I set up the flow the AI Agent follows to work through each question
Next: put numbers on the impact, such as daily time spent preparing data

ai-governance-review.title: Three checks per report
ai-governance-review.sub: Subsidiary AI reports were reviewed by hand, each reviewer differently, so I built a system that judges, recalculates and reconciles them before review.
ai-governance-review.role: Led development of the automated AI governance review and took it live
ai-governance-review.outcome: Live: three review tasks now handled by the system

items.name: Reasonableness
points: The group AI office must review every subsidiary's AI usage report
Reports come from SharePoint, and Azure OpenAI judges the controls and risk treatment plans

items.name: Risk level
points: People used to redo each one by hand, each to their own standard
The system recalculates the risk level, then judges the residual risk left after treatment

items.name: Asset register
points: It checks automatically that each report matches the asset register
With this, the three most labour-heavy review tasks all moved to the system

result.name: Review report
points: It writes a review report and fixes ranked by severity, back into SharePoint
Azure DevOps CI/CD deploys it to Azure Container Apps, tested on every change
Next: time each review to compare before and after

rag-support-bot.title: Little t RAG pipeline
rag-support-bot.sub: Answers were scattered across manuals, so members waited for support; I built a RAG assistant from scratch, and new chunking lifted accuracy from 60% to 85%.
rag-support-bot.role: Team project; I owned the RAG design, vector database and front and back end
rag-support-bot.outcome: Live: accuracy 60% to 85%, answers in about 2 to 3 seconds

items.name: Manuals
points: Members often look up manuals and database usage, and waited for support when they could not find it
RAG over fine-tuning: manuals change often, and RAG only needs the embeddings rebuilt
Documents are parsed with LangExtract

items.name: Semantic chunks
points: Fixed 500-token chunks broke up context, and accuracy sat at 60%
Splitting by paragraph with overlap and chapter metadata raised it to 85%

items.name: Vector DB
points: I compared Pinecone, Weaviate and Chroma, then chose Qdrant
It runs in-house on Docker, so no data leaves the company

items.name: Retrieval
points: Qdrant finds the passages closest to the question
Filtering by category suits the classified lookups common in finance

items.name: Answer
points: The LLM answers from those passages in about 2 to 3 seconds
FastAPI back end and HTML front end; admins maintain the knowledge base themselves

zones.label: Back office: build the index (re-embed when docs change)

notes.text: Knowledge base apart from the model: no retraining

multi-agent-advisory.title: One LLM vs a team
multi-agent-advisory.sub: One AI could not cover every angle or show its reasoning, so five Agents split the work and debate like a fund team, backtested over three years in Zipline.
multi-agent-advisory.role: Contributor: designed each Agent's role and connected TEJ data through MCP
multi-agent-advisory.outcome: A three-year backtest gave the team confidence; results are not public

items.name: Single LLM
points: It struggles to weigh technicals, news sentiment and fundamentals at once
Its advice shows no reasoning, so it cannot be checked
Like one person making every investment call, it has blind spots

items.name: Five-agent team
items.desc: What we built: divide and debate
points: Three analysts each do one job, a debater weighs both sides, a trader gives the signal
LangGraph keeps the flow controllable; I connected TEJ data through MCP
Signals ran through a three-year Zipline backtest, which gave the team confidence in the design

notes.text: Three years of Taiwan stock history

asr-transcription.title: Earnings call to table
asr-transcription.sub: Someone used to type up each earnings call by ear, so I automated it with Whisper: recordings become transcripts, then a key-point table that compares easily.
asr-transcription.role: Contributor: automated the speech-to-text and summary steps
asr-transcription.outcome: Automated and faster; before-and-after numbers still to be measured

items.name: Call recordings
points: Someone used to type up each call by ear, then pull out the key points
Researchers needed points they could compare and quote, not just transcripts

items.name: Speech-to-text
points: The PoC used Whisper to turn call recordings into text
Once that worked, the whole flow was automated

items.name: Automated flow
points: With so many calls, I automated the whole processing flow
Recordings become transcripts automatically, with no handling file by file

items.name: Summary table
points: Each transcript's key points go into a table with fixed fields
Preparing call write-ups now takes less time

items.name: Compare calls
points: Researchers compare key points across companies and quarters directly
Next: time each call to compare before and after automation

zones.label: Now: the whole flow runs itself

notes.text: Listening and typing each call by hand, one at a time
Next: time each call before vs after

financial-statement-vlm.title: OCR vs vision LLM
financial-statement-vlm.sub: Scanned statements are images and classic OCR misses their tables, so I helped switch to cloud Gemini vision, which reads layout and numbers and is now live.
financial-statement-vlm.role: Contributor: helped build the Gemini image reading; exact scope to be added
financial-statement-vlm.outcome: Live; accuracy and time saved to be added

items.name: Classic OCR
points: Some of TEJ's statement sources are scans, images rather than text
Statements live in tables, where every number must map to a line item and period
OCR only turns images into text and cannot read that structure

items.name: Vision LLM
points: Scanned pages go to Gemini, which reads layout, tables and text together
It reads each number with its field and is now live in the statement data flow
Validation details, accuracy and volume: to be added

notes.text: Table lost: numbers lose their line item and period

moda-t-ambassador.title: Locals ask, talent solves
moda-t-ambassador.sub: Rural groups and small firms lacked people who know AI, so as a T Ambassador I worked out solutions with firms and helped them adopt generative AI.
moda-t-ambassador.role: 6th-cohort Digital Youth T Ambassador, helping firms adopt AI
moda-t-ambassador.outcome: Programme completed; firms coached and results to be added

items.name: Locals ask
points: Rural organisations and small firms lack people who know digital tools and AI
In the Ministry of Digital Affairs' programme, firms and groups bring the problems they actually face

items.name: Talent solves
points: I served as a 6th-cohort Digital Youth T Ambassador, working with government on digital change
Together with firms, we turned real problems into digital solutions

result.name: Digital solution
points: Helped firms bring in generative AI and AI-enabled IoT
Also promoted digital transformation policy and engaged the community
Number of firms, industries and concrete results: to be added

notes.text: Goals: digital equity, close the talent gap

tmba-cta-taiex.title: Foundations of a strategy
tmba-cta-taiex.sub: A strategy that cannot be rerun is hard to trust, so I built a reproducible backtest first, tuned it on three metrics, and placed third at the showcase.
tmba-cta-taiex.role: Led development of the TAIEX futures CTA strategy and its backtest framework
tmba-cta-taiex.outcome: Third place at the TMBA 26th algo trading showcase

items.name: TAIEX CTA
points: TMBA's algo trading team builds a strategy every cohort and judges it at term end
I built a CTA strategy on TAIEX futures

items.name: Reproducible test
points: I first built a backtest framework that simulates trades on history
Run the same data twice and get the same result, or the strategy cannot be trusted

items.name: Three metrics
points: Return alone hides how much risk was taken
Sharpe shows return per unit of risk; max drawdown shows the deepest fall

items.name: Optimisation
points: I tuned parameters on the framework and judged them on the three metrics
Backtest period and exact figures: to be added

items.name: Showcase
points: Placed third at the TMBA 26th cohort's algo trading showcase
Next: add the return, Sharpe and max drawdown figures

tmba-event-earnings-call.title: From event to signal
tmba-event-earnings-call.sub: Whether earnings calls offer trades was only a hunch, so I led a Taiwan stock strategy built around them and backtested it on history.
tmba-event-earnings-call.role: Led development and backtesting of the earnings-call event strategy
tmba-event-earnings-call.outcome: Strategy built; entry and exit rules and results to be added

items.name: Earnings call
points: An earnings call is where a company explains its business and outlook
This was my second strategy at TMBA

items.name: Hypothesis
points: Calls release information on operations and outlook
Hypothesis: that information may form a tradable signal

items.name: Strategy
items.desc: Built on the call as event
points: I designed a Taiwan stock strategy with the call as the trading event
Entry and exit rules: to be added

thesis-rag-panel.title: LLM adds explanatory power
thesis-rag-panel.sub: Financial ratios explain little of stock returns, so I built a RAG-LLM that scores reports on six dimensions, lifting explanatory power from 5.14% to 63.73%.

thesis-rag-panel.outcome: Within R² 5.14% to 63.73%; master's degree earned

items.name: Financial vars
points: Research question: can an LLM pull more explanatory signals out of financial reports?
The baseline with classic financial variables only had a within R² of 5.14%
Sample: 592 listed electronics firms over 64 quarters, 37,888 firm-quarters

items.name: LLM scores
points: My RAG-LLM looks up the reports, analyses 101 variables and scores six dimensions
All six scores are significant at the 1% level
A pilot reliability check gave an ICC of 0.759

result.name: Enhanced model
points: Adding the six scores to a fixed-effects panel model raised within R² to 63.73%
Covering 2009Q3 to 2025Q2, supervised by Professors Chou Chih-Lung and Hsieh Chien-Ping

finjourney.title: One-person product loop
finjourney.sub: Spending, investments and insurance sat apart, hiding problems, so I built alone a product that maps it all with an AI adviser, live in under two weeks.
finjourney.role: Solo build: planning, AI tuning, development, deployment and operations
finjourney.outcome: Live in under two weeks with 656 tests; user feedback to be added

items.name: Planning
points: Spending, investments and insurance sat in separate sheets and apps, hiding the problems
Based on the overview diagram in "Investment 101", I split it into ten areas, each from goal to adjustment

items.name: AI tuning
points: AI fixes must follow a JSON schema and pick only from options the system offers
The system checks fields and ranges, then runs a lifetime cash-flow simulation and stress cases
Prompts follow the card the user is viewing, so the AI acts as that card's adviser

items.name: Build and deploy
points: The FastAPI back end does all the maths; the React front end only displays it
An intake API lets other apps send balances and transactions, so nothing is typed by hand
656 automated tests; it runs on my own Mac and goes online through Cloudflare Tunnel

items.name: Operations
points: Sign-up by invite code, one database per user, daily backups kept 14 days
Before using AI, users consent and the version and time are logged; no consent, no AI call
The free tier caps monthly AI use, and only successful answers count

notes.text: Invite codes, daily backups kept 14 days

vibe-edge.title: The backtest iceberg
vibe-edge.sub: AI dreams up strategies faster than anyone can check, so I built a five-layer research platform from scratch, guarded by a validator the AI cannot change.
vibe-edge.role: Solo build: vision, specs, architecture and daily operations
vibe-edge.outcome: Version 0.6.0, all 3,749 tests pass; no live study in the factor library yet

items.name: AI-written nodes
points: Agents produce variants far faster than a person can check them
Every node declares inputs, outputs and parameters in the same manifest.yaml
From zero to version 0.6.0 in 12 weeks and 281 commits

items.name: Paper trading
points: Five layers run from raw data to a paper trade list, with no real money
No live study has yet passed the tests and entered the factor library

items.name: Look-ahead bias
points: A leak sentinel plants a future price gap to see if a node's output changes
Every value carries the date it became public, and the universe is free of survivorship bias

items.name: Overfitting
points: Walk-forward and purged k-fold keep training and test data from overlapping
A promoted cell may open the held-out sample only once

items.name: Multiple testing
points: Every attempt is logged, with m equal to the number of distinct cells in a study
The Deflated Sharpe Ratio discounts results by the number of tries

items.name: Agent isn't judge
points: Checks are fixed in the platform, out of reach of the agents writing nodes
Daily updates went from over an hour to about 100 seconds, with memory under 1 GB
AI spend goes through one global ledger with a hard cap of US$5 a month

notes.text: Five layers: raw data to trade list
No live study in the library yet

fincli.title: Raw data layer
fincli.sub: Much Taiwan market data had no ready tool and was wired by hand, so I built a fetcher that pulls 23 sources every day and stores them exactly as received.
fincli.role: Built tw-fin-scraper and yf-history on my own
fincli.outcome: 23 sources updated daily; old and new fetchers match 141/141

items.name: Never alter
points: Much Taiwan data has no SDK, so each official API or page had to be wired one by one
Rule: store exactly what the source gives, or no one downstream can recover the original

items.name: Backfill first
points: yfinance backfilled 51 Taiwan stocks over 1,699 trading days as raw CSV
When rate-limited I treated HTTP 428 like 429 and retried with exponential backoff

items.name: 23 sources
points: Eight new sources at once, PostgreSQL grew to 26 tables, and runs resume where they stopped
All 143 TWSE and 225 TPEx OpenAPI endpoints are connected
TEJ is reached by browser automation, saving snapshots of 238 tables

items.name: Spec + engine
points: Each dataset is one spec file, fetched by a single engine
Before switching, old and new outputs matched row for row on 141/141 datasets

items.name: Daily operations
points: launchd runs it after each close, with a nightly health check and weekly database backups
If T86 is not out, it retries every 20 minutes; a failed quote fetch waits 5 minutes

items.name: Feeds research
points: For Vibe-Edge I added history on disposition and watch-list stocks, delistings and market holidays
Every table is listed in the data catalogue, and Vibe-Edge reads from it without writing

notes.text: On failure: wait 5 min, up to 3 tries

openstrategy.title: Factor screening funnel
openstrategy.sub: Price moves around earnings calls lacked statistical backing, so my event study found four factors for stock picks; in 2025 they slightly trailed the market.
openstrategy.role: Led the research design, coding and backtesting
openstrategy.outcome: Four significant factors; 2025 Sharpe 0.94 vs market 0.99

items.name: Events & CAR
points: Earnings call events come from TEJ, with the call date as the event day
Abnormal return = stock return minus CAPM expected return; summed, that is CAR

items.name: 9 variables
points: Nine candidates, including a public recording, turnover, prior return, holdings changes and size
Tested with OLS regression, with correlations and VIF to check for overlap

items.name: 4 significant
points: Prior return, days since the last call, company size and book-to-market
Significant over [-3, 3], and the same over [-2, 2]

items.name: 1 composite
points: The four factors become Z-scores, weighted by in-sample Sharpe into one score
Capital follows the score: 1.5x for the top 20%, 0.5x for the bottom 20%

items.name: Out of sample
points: Sharpe 1.21 in training (market 0.39) and 1.37 over the full period (market 0.82)
In 2025 it was 0.94, just under the market's 0.99, missing the target
Next: find why it lagged, and put the full code in the repo
